Front: What is the LIMA finding about SFT?
Back: Almost all knowledge in large language models is learned during pretraining, and only limited instruction tuning data is necessary — 1K examples sufficed, 43% preferred over GPT-4

Front: What did DEITA achieve with only 6K samples?
Back: 7.55 MT-Bench score via complexity/quality/diversity scoring (ICLR 2024); matched SOTA with minimal data

Front: What is the data repetition rule for SFT?
Back: Up to 4 epochs of repeated data is effectively free (negligible loss change); beyond 4 epochs provides zero additional learning benefit. Validated across 400 runs, 900B tokens

Front: What is BFD packing and what does it achieve?
Back: Best-Fit Decreasing packing (ICML 2024): 2x throughput, -20% memory, -58% hallucination, +4.7% reading comprehension, +16.8% context following

Front: What technical requirement does BFD packing have?
Back: Requires flash_attn_varlen_func with cu_seqlens + position_ids to prevent cross-example attention leakage

Front: What is NEFTune and what improvement does it give?
Back: Add noise to embedding vectors during training; LLaMA-2-7B: 29.8% to 64.7% on AlpacaEval. Zero cost, zero complexity — enable by default

Front: What is "train-on-responses-only" in SFT?
Back: Set label=-100 on prompt tokens so model only learns to generate responses, not user prompts; in TRL: assistant_only_loss=True

Front: What is chunked NLL and what does it save?
Back: Drops masked positions BEFORE lm_head matmul, reducing VRAM by 30-50%; set loss_type="chunked_nll" in TRL v1.5.1

Front: What learning rate should you use for 7B full fine-tuning vs LoRA?
Back: Full FT: 2e-5. LoRA: 1-3e-4. Scale down for larger models (70B full FT: 5e-6 to 1e-5)

Front: How many epochs should you train for SFT?
Back: 2-3 for 7B-13B; 1-2 for 70B; 1 for 400B+. Beyond 3 epochs models memorize patterns; the repetition paper proves >4x is worthless

Front: Why is dropout OFF for SFT?
Back: SFT runs are only 1-3 epochs; LoRA "mitigates forgetting more than common regularization techniques such as weight decay and dropout"

Front: Compare LoRA vs full fine-tuning for SFT
Back: LoRA: 3-10x less memory, 0.1-2% params, 95-99% of full FT quality, less forgetting, 7.8x cheaper. Full FT: maximum quality, learns perturbations with rank 10-100x greater

Front: What is FIM (Fill-in-the-Middle) for code?
Back: Move middle span to end of sequence at 50% rate during training; two modes: PSM and SPM. Does NOT harm autoregressive performance. Train all future models with FIM by default

Front: What does process supervision achieve for math SFT?
Back: PRM800K: 800K step-level human labels achieves 78% on MATH; each reasoning step gets a correctness label, dramatically outperforming outcome-only

Front: What is LongLoRA's achievement?
Back: Extends 7B model from 4K to 100K context on a single 8xA100 machine; uses Shifted Sparse Attention during training, dense at inference

Front: What layers MUST be trainable for context extension?
Back: Embedding and normalization layers — LongLoRA found these must be trainable for context extension to work

Front: What is the SFT ceiling problem?
Back: SFT cannot exceed demonstration quality; this is why every top lab follows SFT with RL to raise the ceiling beyond what imitation can achieve

Front: What did Evol-Instruct (WizardLM) achieve?
Back: Superior to human-created instructions; 90% of ChatGPT on 17/29 skills through evolved instruction complexity (ICLR 2024)

Front: What did Orca achieve with synthetic data?
Back: GPT-4 explanation traces enabled a 13B model to surpass Vicuna by 100% on BigBench-Hard

Front: What did Phi-3 achieve?
Back: Textbooks + web filtering at only 3.8B parameters gets 69% MMLU — proving data quality can substitute for model scale

Front: What is the key insight about what SFT teaches?
Back: SFT teaches FORMAT, not CAPABILITY — all knowledge comes from pretraining; SFT just teaches the model to produce it in the right format

Front: What is ORPO's contribution to SFT?
Back: Combines SFT + preference optimization in a single step; "a minor penalty for disfavored style is sufficient" — eliminates need for separate DPO stage

Front: What precision should you always use for SFT?
Back: BF16 — larger dynamic range than FP16, no loss scaling needed, standard on A100/H100

Front: What is the loss function priority hierarchy for SFT?
Back: 1: NEFTune (free +8-35%); 2: Answer-only loss; 3: Chunked NLL (-30-50% VRAM); 4: Standard cross-entropy; 5: ORPO; 6: Label smoothing (rarely needed)

Front: What is OpenAI's unique contribution to post-training?
Back: Proved SFT then RLHF works: 1.3B InstructGPT outperformed 175B GPT-3 in human preference

Front: What is Anthropic's unique contribution to post-training?
Back: Proved no human harm labels needed — constitutional principles suffice for safety alignment

Front: What is DeepSeek's unique contribution to post-training?
Back: Proved minimal SFT + strong RL (GRPO) = cost-efficient SOTA; minimal cold-start SFT sufficient

Front: What is Google's unique contribution to post-training?
Back: Proved distillation can replace SFT entirely for small models (Gemma 2B/9B via knowledge distillation)

Front: What is Meta's SFT scale in Llama 3.1?
Back: 10M+ human annotations with rejection sampling as quality filter; multi-stage pipeline (SFT + Rejection Sampling + PPO + DPO)

Front: What is Qwen 2.5's SFT approach?
Back: 1M+ curated samples via quality scoring across 29 languages, built on 18T token pretraining

Front: What scheduler and warmup should you use for SFT?
Back: Cosine scheduler with 30-step warmup (7B) to 200+ steps (400B+); this is the universal default across StarCoder and most recipes

Front: What is the StarCoder SFT recipe?
Back: lr=5e-5, seq=2048, cosine scheduler, bf16. Full FT: 9hrs/$108 (8xA100). QLoRA: 12.5hrs/$14 (1xA100)

Front: What is MM1's key finding for vision-language SFT?
Back: Image encoder + resolution matters most; connector design is negligible — focus on CLIP quality and resolution, not connector architecture

Front: What effective batch size should you use for SFT?
What is the practitioner recipe for 7B SFT?
Back: ChatML format, BFD packing, CE+NEFTune, LR 2e-5 (full) or 1e-4 (LoRA r=32-64), cosine 30-step warmup, 2-3 epochs, batch 32-128, BF16, gradient checkpointing

Front: How long does 7B SFT take on 10K-50K examples?
Back: 2-6 hours on 1x A100-80GB (QLoRA) or 4-12 hours on 8x A100 (full FT)

Front: What does Self-Rewarding LMs achieve?
Back: Model self-judges its outputs over 3 iterations, beating Claude 2 and GPT-4 (ICML 2024) — demonstrates SFT from self-generated signal

Front: What is DeepSeekMath's pretraining strategy before SFT?
Back: 120B math tokens from Common Crawl for continued pretraining BEFORE SFT — domain-specific pretraining extension

Front: What is the trend replacing expensive human annotation in SFT?
Back: Synthetic data from stronger models (Orca, Phi-3, Evol-Instruct) replacing expensive human annotation

Front: When should you use full FT over LoRA?
Back: When there's a >5% quality gap with LoRA; when model is <7B (full FT is affordable); or when maximum capability ceiling is needed

Front: What weight decay should you use for SFT?
Back: 0 to 0.01 for 7B-13B (StarCoder uses 0.01); 0 for 70B+. LoRA is a better regularizer than weight decay

Front: What does "full FT learns perturbations with rank 10-100x greater than LoRA" mean?
Back: Full fine-tuning can modify the model in higher-rank directions that LoRA's low-rank constraint prevents; this is the 1-5% quality gap between them

Front: What is the recommended approach for tool-use/function-calling SFT?
Back: Train on simple calls, multiple selection, parallel calls, and implicit parameter conversion; formats include OpenAI JSON Schema, Gorilla OpenFunctions, REST API

Front: What does the TRL setting max_length=None do for vision?
Back: Avoids truncating image tokens which can destroy visual information in vision-language training
